correctness.rationale: Independently reimplemented from archived inputs: |PSp6(3)|=4585351680 matches order formula; q=3 is 3 mod 4; stored 49 rows + 25 markers expand to 74 classes with each marker immediately following its parent; E-orders confined to {3,13} so Q(zeta39) trace test is exact; column orthogonality max rel err 4.1e-16 and full row orthonormality hold; exact 39-trace test gives zeros exactly at classes 12,17,18 with t0 nonzero elsewhere; S(1) sanity t0=24|G| holds; power maps give orders 4,6,6, class 12 real and 17/18 an inverse pair; float gap |S|<2e-14 vs min 0.217 elsewhere. Frobenius N=|C|^3/|G|*S(g) then gives 1 not in C^3 for those classes, so e>=4.

originality.rationale: Three-form fused search (literal S6(3)/centralizer parameters; equivalent chi(g)^3/chi(1) structure-constant form; dominance covering-number/class-exponent theorems) plus full-text inspection of the two nearest primaries shows no coverage: Garonzi-Montiijo-Zalesski arXiv:2506.22268 explicitly leaves e(PSp6(q))=3 for q=3 mod 4 open and proves only e<=6 for n>4 and e=3 for PSp4; Guralnick-Malle-Tiep proves Arad-Herzog AB!=C (chi(a)chi(b)=chi(1)chi(c)), a different product question, with S6(q) appearing only there; ATLAS S6(3) page lists generators/representations/maximal subgroups with no exponent data. OpenAIRE outage on two queries was compensated via SerpBase/OpenAlex/Crossref plus direct ATLAS fetch; no UNRESOLVED candidate remains.

value.rationale: TARGET disproof of the admitted universal e(G)=3 claim via the smallest admissible case q=3: three explicit witness classes (order 4 centralizer 2304; inverse pair order 6 centralizer 15552) with certified S(g)=0 give e(PSp6(3))>=4. This changes the explicitly open PSp6 q=3-mod-4 boundary (Garonzi Thm 1.2/6.1), not a type error, vacuity, tiny-instance artifact, direct lookup (tables store values, not S(g)), or arbitrary-parameter fact. As a rigorously established exact invariant of a pre-motivated natural object directly answering Bastos/Garonzi class-exponent questions, it is independently retrievable without requiring a general theorem or full census.
